hero.headline: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use six Republican-leaning congressional districts for midterms
hero.teaser: The decision clears the way for Alabama to remove its second majority-Black district for the 2026 elections.
hero.body:
The Supreme Court has approved Alabama's new congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, clearing the way for Republicans to use the redrawn plan in the upcoming midterm elections. The 6-3 decision represents another significant victory for Republicans following the court's landmark April ruling that weakened a critical provision of the Voting Rights Act.

Alabama's map now contains six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district. The state had challenged a lower court's decision to block the map, arguing that it should be allowed to proceed. The Supreme Court sided with Alabama's position.

This ruling marks the first major test of whether the court's April decision in Louisiana v Callais, which struck down key protections of the Voting Rights Act, would permit states to implement maps that intentionally discriminate against Black voters. The Alabama case demonstrates how that earlier ruling has reshaped the legal landscape surrounding congressional redistricting.

The state's efforts to redraw its map were part of a broader Republican campaign across the South following the April decision. Tennessee implemented a new map eliminating a majority-Black district in Memphis. Louisiana is also preparing to remove a majority-Black district, and South Carolina may follow. Florida's new congressional map, which could provide the GOP four additional seats in the midterms, has also survived initial court challenges.

The Alabama dispute has been contentious. Black voters sued the state in 2021, arguing that its original congressional map diluted their voting power. Federal judges ordered the state to create a new plan with an additional majority-Black district. However, the legislature passed a 2023 map that again eliminated that protection. The Supreme Court ultimately upheld a court-appointed special master's map that included the two majority-Black districts.

The latest Supreme Court decision allows Alabama to move forward with its map that reduces the number of districts where Black voters have a meaningful opportunity to elect candidates of their choice.

The decision has drawn sharp criticism from voting rights advocates. Davin Rosborough, deputy director of the voting rights project at the American Civil Liberties Union, stated that the court's earlier ruling "recognized what we already knew: the Alabama legislature's repeated refusal to provide Black Alabamians with fair representation in Congress is racial discrimination."

Alabama's Republican Attorney General Steve Marshall said he anticipated the outcome. "I am disappointed, but not at all surprised," he said in a statement, adding that he viewed the case as a matter of "when" the state would prevail, not "if."

Civil rights groups have expressed concern that the redistricting efforts across the South represent a return to voter suppression tactics and deliberately deny Black voters a voice in the political process.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes as tensions escalate in Gulf
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have exchanged fresh military strikes, undermining diplomatic efforts to reach a new ceasefire agreement between the two nations. The escalation began when US forces fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to break through an American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The US military subsequently reported that it repelled Iranian attacks in the region and struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it attacked the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones in retaliation for the strike on Qeshm. The US military's Central Command denied that this Iranian attack succeeded. The exchange of strikes represents a significant setback for ceasefire negotiations, which had been ongoing between Washington and Tehran.

Despite the military escalation, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed during his first Senate Foreign Relations Committee appearance that a deal with Tehran remained within reach. Rubio stated that Iran had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program that it had previously refused to discuss even a month earlier.

The Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, took a harder line on the agreement. He stated that "the ceasefire between Iran and the US is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. Its violation on one front is a violation of the ceasefire on all fronts. The US and Israel are responsible for the consequences of any violation."

The latest military exchange underscores the lack of political progress in resolving the broader Middle East crisis, despite optimistic claims from US officials. The Strait of Hormuz, where the tanker incident occurred, is a strategically vital global shipping route and energy corridor. Control over the waterway and the surrounding region remains a critical point of contention between the two countries.

The targeting of American forces in Bahrain and the US response on Iranian territory demonstrates the widening geographic scope of the confrontation. Both nations appear entrenched in their positions, with military action continuing even as diplomatic channels remain nominally open. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing strikes highlight the fragile security situation in the Gulf.

The failure to make progress in ceasefire negotiations, combined with continued military operations, suggests that tensions between the United States and Iran will likely persist. With both sides claiming defensive justifications for their actions and disagreeing on fundamental ceasefire terms, prospects for immediate de-escalation appear limited. The situation demonstrates how quickly military confrontation can overwhelm diplomatic efforts in this volatile region.

cards.headline: Trump administration drops $1.8 billion payout fund after GOP revolt
cards.teaser: The Justice Department abandoned a proposed fund following opposition from Republican lawmakers.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department will not proceed with a proposed $1.8 billion compensation fund. The decision followed pushback from top Republican lawmakers against the initiative, which the administration had previously backed.

The reversal marks a significant policy shift for the Trump administration, as internal GOP opposition proved influential in the final outcome.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise as U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes During Stalled Negotiations
cards.teaser: Hostilities continued between the two countries as peace talks reached an impasse, sending oil prices higher.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran launched fresh military strikes against each other as ceasefire negotiations stalled. American aircraft targeted Iranian military sites, including locations on Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran responded by attacking U.S. air bases in the Gulf region.

Oil prices climbed following the escalated hostilities, driven by concerns over potential supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed military activity contrasted with statements that diplomatic discussions remained ongoing between the countries.

cards.headline: Canada requests 16-year extension of North American trade pact
cards.teaser: The Canadian trade minister formally asked the US and Mexico to renew the USMCA deal.
cards.body:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the North American free trade agreement. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc sent a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico proposing that the three countries extend the USMCA trade deal.

The USMCA, which replaced NAFTA, governs trade relations among the three North American nations. The request comes as the agreement enters its review period.

cards.headline: Russian war intensity increases as public discourse shifts after four years
cards.teaser: Russia has intensified attacks in Ukraine, but prolonged conflict is causing concern among Putin loyalists.
cards.body:
Russia has intensified its military attacks on Ukraine more than four years into the war. A recent massive aerial assault on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities killed at least 22 civilians and wounded 138 others, according to officials.

Despite the ongoing conflict, President Vladimir Putin has maintained an uncompromising stance and shown no willingness to pursue a negotiated settlement. The prolonged war and its mounting costs are generating concern even among Putin's supporters within Russia, prompting discussion about the conflict in a country where public discourse on the war has been heavily restricted since the invasion began.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as partial Hezbollah truce continues
cards.teaser: Israel maintained military operations in southern Lebanon but has not struck Beirut since a US-announced deal.
cards.body:
Israel continued its military campaign in southern Lebanon while a partial truce with Hezbollah held in other areas. Israeli forces have not struck the capital city of Beirut following a deal announced by the United States.

The arrangement represents a limited de-escalation in the conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group. While operations continue in the south, the pause in strikes on Beirut suggests both parties are observing at least some elements of the agreement brokered by American officials.

cards.headline: Iran targets US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait in failed attacks
cards.teaser: Iran aimed strikes at American air bases in the Gulf, but the attacks were shot down or failed.
cards.body:
Iran launched missile and drone strikes targeting US air bases in Bahrain and Kuwait. The US military said the attacks were either intercepted or failed to reach their targets, with no damage or casualties reported at the bases.

The US responded with strikes of its own, including a Hellfire missile that disabled a tanker near the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on sites on Iran's Qeshm Island. The escalation comes as ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran have stalled.

cards.headline: Protests grow in Albania over Kushner-connected resort development
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury resorts on the Adriatic Sea have sparked demonstrations reflecting broader government frustrations.
cards.body:
Protests in Albania have intensified over plans for luxury resort developments on the Adriatic Sea linked to Jared Kushner. The proposed projects have long raised concerns among environmental groups worried about the impact on coastal ecosystems and public access to beaches.

The demonstrations have evolved beyond environmental concerns to become a focal point for wider dissatisfaction with the Albanian government. Citizens are using the resort controversy to express frustration with government policies and priorities, making the development plans a symbol of larger governance issues in the country.

cards.headline: Court ruling delays US Ebola quarantine facility in Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court blocked the Trump administration's proposed quarantine unit for Americans exposed to the virus.
cards.body:
A court in Kenya issued a ruling that further delayed the Trump administration's plans to build an Ebola quarantine facility in the country. The proposed unit would be located at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki, about 120 miles from Nairobi, and would house Americans exposed to the virus but not yet symptomatic.

The project has faced strong local opposition. Residents of the town near the proposed site have criticized the plan, arguing that quarantines should occur in people's home countries. They express concern about exposure to the virus in Kenya, which has no known Ebola cases, and view the proposal as reflecting double standards by the US.

hero.headline: US launches new strikes on Iran as ceasefire talks stall
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have resumed military strikes against each other after negotiations aimed at establishing a lasting ceasefire broke down. The escalation marks a critical failure in diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between Washington and Tehran.

The breakdown came as Iran suspended participation in peace talks, citing Israel's military operations in Lebanon as a violation of ceasefire terms. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that "the ceasefire between Iran and the US is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. Its violation on one front is a violation of the ceasefire on all fronts."

US forces fired a Hellfire missile to disable a tanker attempting to break through the American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The US military then reported repelling Iranian retaliatory attacks in the region and striking Iranian sites on Qeshm Island.

Iran responded by announcing it had targeted a military base in Kuwait that it claimed was involved in US operations. The Iranian military command issued warnings to residents of northern Israel, threatening attacks if Israel proceeded with strikes on Beirut and its southern suburbs.

The collapse of negotiations represents a significant setback after discussions had appeared to approach agreement on Friday. President Donald Trump pulled back from a preliminary deal, demanding revisions to the outline agreement. Trump stated he was not opposed to halting talks, telling NBC News that "going silent would be very good." However, he indicated the US would maintain its blockade on Iranian ports rather than launch immediate military escalation.

Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, contended that the US blockade and Israeli actions in Lebanon constituted "clear evidence of US non-compliance" with the ceasefire terms. He warned that "every choice has a price, and the bill comes due."

The ceasefire had technically been in effect since early April, though the US and Iran had exchanged strikes several times during this period. The tensions have raised global concerns, with oil prices climbing close to 100 dollars per barrel.

European leaders expressed alarm at the deteriorating situation. French President Emmanuel Macron spoke with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, Trump, and major Arab leaders on Sunday, urging recognition of the necessity for a ceasefire in Lebanon and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to resume oil transit.

Iran's military command warned that if attacks on Beirut continued, it would request the Houthis in Yemen to establish a second shipping blockade at the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.

The situation now stands at a critical juncture, with both nations demonstrating willingness to conduct military operations and raising the risk of broader regional conflict involving multiple actors with interests in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Trump administration drops $1.8 billion payout fund after GOP revolt
cards.teaser: The Justice Department abandoned a proposed fund following opposition from Republican lawmakers.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department will not proceed with a proposed $1.8 billion compensation fund. The decision followed pushback from top Republican lawmakers against the initiative, which the administration had previously backed.

The reversal marks a significant policy shift for the Trump administration, as internal GOP opposition proved influential in the final outcome.

cards.headline: Man barricades himself with hostages inside California bank amid bomb threat
cards.teaser: Police in Bakersfield are negotiating with a man who took hostages at a Chase Bank branch.
cards.body:
A man barricaded himself inside a Chase Bank in downtown Bakersfield, California, with multiple hostages on Tuesday. According to police, the man had a bomb strapped to his body during the incident.

Law enforcement responded to the scene and began negotiations. One hostage was safely released, and police reported that the remaining people inside the bank were in good health. Authorities evacuated the surrounding downtown area as a precaution.

cards.headline: Supreme Court reinstates Republican-drawn Alabama congressional map
cards.teaser: The ruling means Alabama's midterm elections will use districts favoring Republicans six to one.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court reinstated Alabama's congressional district map in a 6-3 decision, allowing the state to use redrawn boundaries for the 2026 midterm elections. The map eliminates one of Alabama's two majority-Black districts, resulting in six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.

The ruling overturned a lower court decision that had blocked the map and represents a significant victory for Republicans. Legal experts have noted this decision follows the Court's earlier ruling that struck down a critical provision of the Voting Rights Act, further limiting protections for Black voters in redistricting cases.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in the race to lead New Mexico.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico's gubernatorial race. The former Interior Secretary under the Biden administration will be the Democratic nominee in the general election.

Haaland previously served in Congress representing New Mexico before joining the Cabinet. She will face a Republican opponent in the general election to determine the state's next governor.

cards.headline: Paralympic champion Josh Turek wins Iowa Republican Senate primary
cards.teaser: The gold medalist secured the GOP nomination with backing from party establishment figures.
cards.body:
Josh Turek, a Paralympic gold medalist, won the Republican primary for US Senate in Iowa with support from establishment Republicans. Turek will face the Democratic nominee in the general election for the Senate seat. Some reporting also indicated that Representative Ashley Hinson received Trump's endorsement and secured a Senate nomination, though details about multiple races were not fully clear.

Iowa held primary elections that will determine the candidates for several key races in the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats are targeting the Republican-held Senate seat as a potential pickup opportunity. The general election will test whether Iowa remains reliably Republican or if Democrats can compete in statewide races.

cards.headline: Democrat Rebecca Bennett to challenge absent Rep. Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey
cards.teaser: The former Navy pilot won the Democratic primary to face the congressman who has not been seen since March.
cards.body:
Rebecca Bennett, a former Navy pilot and Democrat, won her party's primary to challenge Republican Representative Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey's most contested House district. Kean has been absent from Congress and has not been seen publicly since March, according to investigations by news organizations.

Despite his absence, Kean received an endorsement from former President Trump. The New York Times conducted an extensive search for the congressman and documented his disappearance from public view. Bennett will attempt to flip the competitive district in a race that has drawn national attention due to the incumbent's mysterious absence from his duties.

hero.headline: SpaceX Plans to Sell 555.6 Million Shares at $135 in Historic IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX announced plans for a major initial public offering, with the company targeting a valuation of approximately $1.75 trillion. The space company intends to sell 555.6 million shares at $135 per share in an all-primary offering, meaning shares will come directly from SpaceX rather than from existing investors selling their stakes.

The proposed valuation has raised concerns among market analysts. Morningstar assessed SpaceX's worth at $780 billion, significantly less than half the company's IPO target. This substantial gap between SpaceX's asking price and independent valuations presents a challenge for potential investors evaluating the stock ahead of trading.

Over the past two decades, SpaceX has reshaped the aerospace sector. The company now dominates commercial satellite launch services and holds contracts to transport astronauts to the International Space Station. SpaceX operates Starlink, its satellite internet service, and continues developing Starship, a rocket system designed for lunar and Martian missions. The company's reusable rocket technology has significantly lowered launch expenses and increased the frequency of missions.

The IPO raises strategic questions about SpaceX's direction as a public company. Currently, SpaceX generates revenue from government contracts, commercial launches, and Starlink subscriptions. Industry observers are uncertain whether the company will maintain its focus on launch services or shift toward alternative revenue sources under public ownership.

Becoming a publicly traded company will fundamentally change how SpaceX operates. The firm will face mandatory quarterly earnings reports and shareholder expectations that may conflict with the extended development timelines SpaceX pursued as a private entity. Founder Elon Musk has historically been reluctant to take his companies public, previously expressing concerns that short-term investor pressure undermines ambitious technological goals. His decision to pursue an IPO at this time suggests either a capital requirement for ongoing projects or pressure from early investors seeking liquidity opportunities.

The timing of the IPO also reflects broader market dynamics. Other major technology and energy companies have recently pursued significant capital raises. Alphabet announced plans to raise up to $80 billion through equity sales to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure investments. Anthropic, an AI company, plans to offer public share sales later this year with a valuation approaching $1 trillion.

SpaceX's historic IPO comes at a moment when large technology companies are aggressively pursuing capital to support emerging business priorities, particularly in artificial intelligence and space technology. The company's transition from private to public ownership will test whether SpaceX can balance investor expectations with its ambitious long-term development goals in space exploration and satellite communications.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over $1 Billion Deal to Halt Offshore Wind Farm
cards.teaser: A coalition of states filed suit after the administration paid a French company nearly $1 billion to abandon an offshore wind project.
cards.body:
Seven states, including New York, have filed a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration's decision to pay French energy company TotalEnergies approximately $1 billion to cancel an offshore wind farm project. The states argue the administration lacked authority to use federal funds to terminate the renewable energy development.

The legal challenge centers on whether the agreement violates established environmental and energy policies. The offshore wind farm was intended to generate electricity for coastal communities before the administration negotiated its cancellation through the financial settlement with TotalEnergies.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: The network dismissed the former CBS Evening News anchor after months of staff tensions with editor in chief Bari Weiss.
cards.body:
CBS News removed Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes as part of a broader overhaul that also affected the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. The changes came amid tensions between staff and Bari Weiss, the network's editor in chief.

During a staff meeting, Pelley directly criticized Weiss and CBS News leadership over the dismissals. Pelley, a veteran correspondent who previously anchored the CBS Evening News, expressed strong opposition to the network's decisions regarding the show's personnel.

cards.headline: Container Ship Struck by Projectiles in Iraqi Port Amid Regional Tensions
cards.teaser: An MSC vessel was hit by two projectiles at an Iraqi port as the U.S. and Iran attempt to negotiate reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
A ship owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company was struck by two projectiles while docked at an Iraqi port. The attack occurred as the United States and Iran conduct negotiations aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments.

The incident highlights ongoing risks to commercial shipping in the region despite diplomatic efforts. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed to traffic, affecting energy markets and supply chains. Neither country has announced progress in the talks aimed at restoring access to the strategic passage.

cards.headline: Japan's Nikkei Index Reaches Record High Above 68,000
cards.teaser: The Tokyo stock benchmark hit a new milestone as technology stocks rallied despite tensions in the Middle East.
cards.body:
The Nikkei 225 index climbed above 68,000 for the first time, marking a new record high. Japanese stocks benefited from gains in U.S. technology shares, with the index rising by as much as 1,000 points during the trading session.

The rally reflected broader momentum in global equity markets, as Wall Street indexes also reached new record levels in recent sessions. This optimism carried over to Asian markets, pushing the Nikkei to its historic peak.

cards.headline: Colorado Tightens Regulations on Uber and Lyft Following Safety Investigation
cards.teaser: The state enacted a law increasing oversight of ride-hailing companies after a report found Uber received more assault complaints than publicly disclosed.
cards.body:
Colorado passed legislation tightening scrutiny of Uber and Lyft operations within the state. The law followed a New York Times investigation that revealed Uber received reports of sexual assault or sexual misconduct far more frequently than the company had publicly acknowledged.

The new regulations increase state oversight of ride-hailing platforms' safety practices and reporting requirements. The Times investigation documented a gap between internal company records and public disclosures about passenger and driver safety incidents. Colorado becomes one of the first states to respond legislatively to the findings.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches Scout, an AI assistant the company aims to make users rely on constantly
hero.body:
Microsoft introduced Scout, a new AI assistant designed to operate continuously in the background of users' work lives. Internal documents obtained by 404 Media reveal the company's goal is to make people dependent on the technology, which functions as an always-on personal agent. The assistant was announced at Microsoft's Build developer conference alongside other AI initiatives.

Scout operates differently from traditional software by working like an executive assistant that never stops monitoring and responding to user needs. The system draws on Microsoft's partnership with OpenAI, using technology the company describes as OpenClaw-inspired. Unlike conventional applications that users open and close, Scout runs persistently to anticipate needs and automate tasks.

The company also announced Work IQ APIs, which allow developers to integrate Scout's capabilities into their own applications. Microsoft is positioning the assistant as a coworker rather than a tool, representing a shift in how the company envisions people interacting with their computers. Bloomberg reported the assistant functions similarly to executive support staff, handling scheduling, communications, and task management.

The internal documents showing Microsoft's intention to create user dependence on Scout have raised questions about the company's approach to AI adoption. The phrasing suggests Microsoft views habitual reliance on the assistant as a feature rather than a concern. WIRED described Scout as an AI coworker that never logs off, emphasizing its persistent presence in the digital workspace.

The announcement comes as Microsoft seeks to reduce its reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. CNBC reported the company unveiled new AI models at Build 2026 designed to give developers more options beyond OpenAI's technology. Microsoft also used the conference to promote Windows as a trusted development platform, suggesting Scout and related AI tools will be tightly integrated with the operating system. The assistant represents Microsoft's bet that the future of computing involves constant AI mediation rather than discrete application use.

cards.headline: Microsoft unveils Project Solara, an Android OS built around AI agents instead of apps
cards.teaser: Microsoft introduced an Android-based operating system designed for AI agents rather than traditional applications.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system that replaces the traditional app-focused interface with an agent-centric design. The system represents Microsoft's attempt to enter the mobile operating system market through a fundamentally different approach than conventional smartphone software.

The company framed Project Solara as a response to having missed the boat on app-based mobile ecosystems. Rather than competing directly with iOS and Android's application models, Microsoft is building an operating system where AI agents perform tasks on behalf of users without requiring discrete app launches.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Linux tools and RTX Spark desktop for Windows developers
cards.teaser: Microsoft revealed new developer tools at Build, including Linux integration and a hardware product.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced new tools for Windows developers at its Build conference, including enhanced Linux capabilities and a hardware product called RTX Spark desktop. The announcements represent Microsoft's continued efforts to make Windows a more attractive platform for software development.

The company highlighted several software improvements alongside one hardware announcement. The moves are part of Microsoft's broader strategy to position Windows as the trusted platform for development, competing with macOS and Linux-based systems that have gained popularity among programmers.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera nears $300 million funding round at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Cyera is raising capital at 80 times its annual recurring revenue despite not yet turning a profit.
cards.body:
Cyera is closing in on a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners, which would value the cybersecurity company at $12 billion. This represents an 80 times multiple of the company's annual recurring revenue.

The valuation reflects strong investor confidence in the cybersecurity sector and Cyera's growth prospects, despite the company currently operating at a loss.

cards.headline: PlayStation reveals new details on Marvel's Wolverine game at State of Play event
cards.teaser: Sony showed gameplay footage and story details for the upcoming Wolverine title from Insomniac Games.
cards.body:
Sony showcased Marvel's Wolverine during its State of Play event on June 2nd, 2026. Insomniac Games' PS5 exclusive launches September 15th. The presentation featured gameplay footage of Logan in his iconic yellow outfit, demonstrating combat encounters where he uses his claws to fight enemies.

The demo highlighted the game's violent combat style as players navigate through enemy encounters with Wolverine's signature blade attacks.

cards.headline: Santa Monica Studio announces God of War Laufey starring Kratos' wife Faye
cards.teaser: The God of War series shifts protagonists from Kratos to his late wife in a new game.
cards.body:
Sony unveiled God of War Laufey, the next installment in the franchise from Santa Monica Studio. The game shifts focus to Faye, Kratos' wife, as the protagonist instead of the series' traditional lead. The reveal came during Sony's State of Play presentation.

The new title is confirmed for PlayStation 5, though a release date has not yet been announced. Creators discussed their decision to move away from Kratos for this entry during the showcase.

cards.headline: Ubisoft announces Rayman Legends Retold, a 3D remake launching October 1
cards.teaser: The 2D platformer is being rebuilt in three dimensions and will support ray tracing on Nintendo's new console.
cards.body:
Ubisoft revealed Rayman Legends Retold, a 3D remake of the 2013 platformer set to release October 1. Game Informer reported playing the remake for two hours and called the original the best Rayman game. The remake will launch on PlayStation 5 and other platforms.

Video Games Chronicle reported the game will run at 60 frames per second with ray tracing on Nintendo Switch 2, with developers saying performance is

hero.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett from Browns in blockbuster trade
hero.body:
The Los Angeles Rams acquired star edge rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in a major trade on Monday, sending linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to Cleveland in the deal.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since being drafted first overall by the Browns in 2017, he has established himself as one of the league's premier defensive players. He holds the record for most sacks (125.5), pressures (413), and tackles for loss (149) among players selected in that draft class. In 2025, Garrett set the single-season sacks record with 23.

The star pass rusher had requested a trade from the Browns in 2024 after the team finished with a 3-14 record. Seeking a fresh start with a championship contender, Garrett signed a four-year, $160 million extension with Cleveland a month later that made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal includes $122.8 million in guaranteed money and averages $40 million annually.

Despite Garrett's individual excellence, the Browns finished 2025 with a 5-12 record and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year. General manager Andrew Berry said the team faced a difficult decision. "As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said after announcing the trade.

The contract modifications proved essential to completing the deal. The Browns and Garrett agreed to defer option payments over the 2026-28 seasons, pushing a $10 million payment due in March to the start of the regular season.

The Rams, coming off a loss to the eventual champion Seattle Seahawks in the NFC championship game, add another elite defensive weapon to their roster. This marks the first time the reigning AP NFL MVP and Defensive Player of the Year will be teammates, with quarterback Matthew Stafford winning his first MVP award last season.

Verse, the 25-year-old linebacker sent to Cleveland, was a first-round pick by the Rams in 2024. He earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors while recording 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss. The Browns also received a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection.

The Rams have a track record of ambitious trades. In 2021, they swapped Jared Goff to the Detroit Lions to acquire Matthew Stafford, who led Los Angeles to a Super Bowl victory in his first season with the team.

cards.headline: Drake London signs four-year, $141 million extension with Falcons
cards.teaser: The Atlanta Falcons and wide receiver Drake London agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $141 million.
cards.body:
The Atlanta Falcons secured Drake London with a four-year, $141 million contract extension, his agent confirmed. The deal keeps the team's top receiver under contract through the 2029 season and represents one of the larger investments in a wide receiver this offseason.

London has emerged as the Falcons' primary offensive weapon since entering the league. NFL Network reported the agreement, which was finalized after negotiations between the team and London's representation. The extension prevents London from reaching free agency and provides Atlanta with stability at the receiver position as the team builds its offense around him.

cards.headline: Hurricanes take early lead over Golden Knights in Stanley Cup Final opener
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes jumped to a fast start against the Vegas Golden Knights in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Carolina's Nikolaj Ehlers helped the Hurricanes build an early advantage in the opening game of the Stanley Cup Final against Vegas. The series marks Carolina's bid for its first championship since 2006, while the Golden Knights seek their second title in franchise history.

The game aired live on ABC, with watch parties organized across Las Vegas for fans following the series. ESPN analysts had offered predictions on the matchup before the puck dropped, weighing the strengths of both teams. The series represents the culmination of the 2026 NHL playoffs, with both clubs having navigated through three previous rounds to reach the final.

cards.headline: Manchester United agree to $45 million deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson
cards.teaser: Manchester United reached an agreement with Atalanta to sign Brazilian midfielder Ederson for approximately $45 million.
cards.body:
Atalanta's 26-year-old Brazilian midfielder Éderson is set to become Michael Carrick's first signing as Manchester United manager. The clubs have agreed on a deal worth £35 million (€40.5m), with the player having already agreed personal terms on a contract through 2030.

Éderson was identified by Carrick and director of football Jason Wilcox as a replacement for Casemiro, who departed United after his contract expired. The transfer addresses the club's midfield reinforcement needs during the summer window.

cards.headline: Transfer Milan Momcilovic to arrive at Kentucky after committing to Wildcats
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic is scheduled to arrive at Kentucky, where he transferred after entering the portal.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, ranked as the top transfer in college basketball, is set to arrive at Kentucky on a specific date after choosing the Wildcats over other programs. The decision gives head coach Mark Pope a significant recruiting victory in the transfer portal and prompted Kentucky's entry into the CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 rankings.

Momcilovic previously played at Iowa State, where he established himself as one of the top players in the transfer market. His commitment followed what WDRB described as a high-stakes recruitment involving substantial financial considerations. ESPN and USA Today both highlighted the transfer as one of the most significant portal moves of the offseason, with Momcilovic expected to play a central role in Kentucky's lineup.

cards.headline: Chicago mayor says Bears will remain in city despite stadium bill setback
cards.teaser: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson expressed confidence the Bears will stay in the city after a $55 billion Illinois budget passed without a stadium provision.
cards.body:
Mayor Brandon Johnson expressed confidence that the Chicago Bears will stay in the city following the Illinois legislature's passage of a $55 billion budget that excluded stadium funding. Johnson cited his legislative successes in Springfield as evidence that Chicago remains a viable option for the franchise.

The Bears released a statement after the budget vote failed to include provisions they had sought. Lawmakers suggested the team's lobbying approach may have contributed to the defeat of a broader megaprojects bill that could have supported the stadium deal. The franchise is now evaluating its options regarding Chicago's future.

cards.headline: Zverev advances to French Open semifinals after defeating Jodar
cards.teaser: Alexander Z
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev secured his place in the French Open semifinals with a comprehensive quarter-final victory over teenager Rafael Jodar. The win keeps the German star's pursuit of an elusive Grand Slam title alive at Roland Garros.

Zverev will now face Mensik in the last four, continuing his campaign for his first major championship.

hero.headline: Singer Peabo Bryson Dies at 75
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning singer known for his soaring ballads and Disney film duets, has died at 75. The soul and R&B artist passed away, according to multiple reports citing CBS News and Variety.

Bryson achieved widespread fame for his performances on two Disney animated film soundtracks. He recorded "Beauty and the Beast" with Celine Dion for the 1991 film and "A Whole New World" with Regina Belle for the 1992 film Aladdin. Both songs became international hits and earned him Grammy Awards. His rich tenor voice and romantic delivery made him a defining artist of ballad-driven R&B.

Beyond his Disney work, Bryson built a career spanning decades with hits including "Im So Into You" and "Let the Feeling Flow." The New York Times described him as the "Voice of Love" in recognition of his signature romantic style. His music crossed over from R&B charts to mainstream pop, establishing him as one of the most recognizable voices in American popular music from the 1970s through the 1990s.

Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens led public tributes following news of Bryson's death, according to CBS News. The singer's connection to Atlanta and the broader music community prompted an outpouring of remembrances from fans and fellow artists. His influence on R&B vocal performance and his role in bringing soul music to film soundtracks left a lasting mark on American entertainment.

Bryson's death removes one of the most distinctive voices from the generation of soul and R&B singers who defined the sound of romantic ballads in late 20th-century American music. His Disney recordings introduced his vocal style to global audiences and remain among the most recognized songs in animated film history.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley From 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The veteran correspondent was terminated after a public argument with the news program's new executive producer.
cards.body:
CBS News has terminated Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at 60 Minutes, following a heated clash with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton during a staff meeting on Monday. The confrontation occurred days after Bilton, a former tech journalist, was installed in the role by CBS editorial chief Bari Weiss.

Pelley criticized management's decision to fire the show's previous executive producer, executive editor, and two fellow correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega, as part of a broader overhaul. After the public argument, network executives and Pelley concluded they could not continue working together. The departures leave 60 Minutes with three remaining correspondents.

cards.headline: South Park Creator Criticizes President Trump in Television Academy Honors Video
cards.teaser: Trey Parker said the president thinks his job is to be the Joker during a discussion about the animated series.
cards.body:
South Park creator Trey Parker made pointed remarks about President Donald Trump during a video segment for the 19th Television Academy Honors, which aired May 20. Parker said Trump believes his job is to be the Joker, explaining why he and co-creator Matt Stone made the president a main character in the latest season of their animated series.

Parker and Stone discussed their role in comedy and their approach to political satire in the recorded segment. The creators have previously addressed political figures in South Park, and their decision to feature Trump prominently in the most recent season reflected their view of his approach to the presidency.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Credits Zendaya as a Lifeline in Hollywood Career
cards.teaser: The actor said he could not imagine doing his work without her support.
cards.body:
Tom Holland described Zendaya as a lifeline while discussing his career in Hollywood. The actor said he could not imagine doing what he does without her, highlighting the importance of their relationship both personally and professionally.

Holland also praised Zendaya's work in the HBO series Euphoria and the upcoming film The Odyssey. His comments reflected the public support the two actors have shown for each other's careers since they began working together on Spider-Man films.

cards.headline: NBC Cancels The Hunting Party After Two Seasons
cards.teaser: The crime drama starring Melissa Roxburgh will be shopped to other networks.
cards.body:
NBC has ended The Hunting Party after two seasons. The crime drama, which concluded on May 7, featured Melissa Roxburgh in the lead role as FBI profiler Bex Henderson. The show centered on a team of investigators working to apprehend dangerous criminals.

The producers intend to pitch the series to other networks and streaming services in hopes of finding it a new home. The cancellation reflects NBC's ongoing adjustments to its programming slate as the network prepares for the upcoming television season.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Begins Eighth Season
cards.teaser: The reality dating competition returns with a new cast of contestants.
cards.body:
Love Island USA premiered its eighth season with a new cast of singles competing for romance and a cash prize in a tropical villa setting. The reality dating competition continues to draw large audiences with its format centered on coupling, recoupling, and public voting that determines which pairs advance through the competition.

Fans can watch the new season and meet the 2026 islanders through multiple platforms. USA Today and Yahoo both covered the cast reveal and provided details on the episode release schedule and viewing options for the show.

cards.headline: JioHotstar Expands AI Division With 75 New Positions
cards.teaser: India's largest streaming platform is building out artificial intelligence capabilities across engineering and production.
cards.body:
India's largest streaming service JioHotstar is hiring more than 75 people to build out a dedicated artificial intelligence division. The company announced the expansion Wednesday with open positions across engineering, production automation, and creative technology.

JioHotstar is leveraging India's multilingual market and technical workforce as a foundation for developing AI technology. The company views artificial intelligence as essential to its content delivery and production operations moving forward.

hero.headline: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use six Republican-leaning congressional districts for midterms
hero.teaser: The decision clears the way for Alabama to remove its second majority-Black district for the 2026 elections.
hero.body:
The Supreme Court has approved Alabama's new congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, clearing the way for Republicans to use the redrawn plan in the upcoming midterm elections. The 6-3 decision represents another significant victory for Republicans following the court's landmark April ruling that weakened a critical provision of the Voting Rights Act.

Alabama's map now contains six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district. The state had challenged a lower court's decision to block the map, arguing that it should be allowed to proceed. The Supreme Court sided with Alabama's position.

This ruling marks the first major test of whether the court's April decision in Louisiana v Callais, which struck down key protections of the Voting Rights Act, would permit states to implement maps that intentionally discriminate against Black voters. The Alabama case demonstrates how that earlier ruling has reshaped the legal landscape surrounding congressional redistricting.

The state's efforts to redraw its map were part of a broader Republican campaign across the South following the April decision. Tennessee implemented a new map eliminating a majority-Black district in Memphis. Louisiana is also preparing to remove a majority-Black district, and South Carolina may follow. Florida's new congressional map, which could provide the GOP four additional seats in the midterms, has also survived initial court challenges.

The Alabama dispute has been contentious. Black voters sued the state in 2021, arguing that its original congressional map diluted their voting power. Federal judges ordered the state to create a new plan with an additional majority-Black district. However, the legislature passed a 2023 map that again eliminated that protection. The Supreme Court ultimately upheld a court-appointed special master's map that included the two majority-Black districts.

The latest Supreme Court decision allows Alabama to move forward with its map that reduces the number of districts where Black voters have a meaningful opportunity to elect candidates of their choice.

The decision has drawn sharp criticism from voting rights advocates. Davin Rosborough, deputy director of the voting rights project at the American Civil Liberties Union, stated that the court's earlier ruling "recognized what we already knew: the Alabama legislature's repeated refusal to provide Black Alabamians with fair representation in Congress is racial discrimination."

Alabama's Republican Attorney General Steve Marshall said he anticipated the outcome. "I am disappointed, but not at all surprised," he said in a statement, adding that he viewed the case as a matter of "when" the state would prevail, not "if."

Civil rights groups have expressed concern that the redistricting efforts across the South represent a return to voter suppression tactics and deliberately deny Black voters a voice in the political process.

cards.headline: US military shoots down Iranian missiles and drones, strikes targets in Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: US forces shot down multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones and conducted strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday in response to attem.
cards.body:
US Central Command shot down multiple Iranian ballistic missiles and drones launched in an attempted attack on Tuesday. Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait and Bahrain failed to reach their targets, while US forces intercepted additional Iranian aircraft before they could strike American forces or regional partners.

In response, American aircraft struck Iranian military sites on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping chokepoint. The military action occurred as peace negotiations between the US and Iran remained stalled, marking an escalation in direct exchanges between the two countries amid rising tensions across the Middle East.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary in New Mexico governor race
cards.teaser: The former Interior Secretary could become the first Native American woman elected governor.
cards.body:
Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor, the race to succeed Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham. If elected in November, Haaland would become the first Native American woman to serve as a state governor.

Haaland previously served in Congress before joining President Biden's cabinet as Interior Secretary.

cards.headline: Canada calls for renewal of North American free-trade agreement
cards.teaser: The proposal comes amid ongoing economic and political pressure from the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Canada is urging the United States and Mexico to renew their North American free-trade agreement for another 16 years. Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc sent letters to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Mexico's Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard requesting the renewal of the USMCA trade deal.

The request comes as the Trump administration has applied economic and political pressure on both neighboring countries. The three-nation trade agreement governs commerce across North America.

cards.headline: California governor primary results may take days or weeks to finalize
cards.teaser: Mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day are valid if they arrive by June 9.
cards.body:
Updated Card Text

California's primary elections, including the competitive gubernatorial race, face a notoriously slow vote-counting system that could delay results for days or weeks. County election offices are expected to be overwhelmed with last-minute absentee ballots and will need to undertake a painstaking ballot-by-ballot verification process.

Governor Gavin Newsom has expressed concern that prolonged delays in the tightest races could allow "election lies" to take hold. The state's 58 county elections offices will manage the counting process after polls close on Election Day.

cards.headline: Ashley Hinson and Josh Turek win Iowa Senate primaries
cards.teaser: The two candidates will compete for Senator Joni Ernst's seat in November.
cards.body:
Representative Ashley Hinson won the Republican primary for Iowa's Senate seat, while state Representative Josh Turek secured the Democratic nomination. The two will face off in November to fill the seat being vacated by retiring Senator Joni Ernst.

Turek, a two-time Paralympic gold medalist, defeated his Democratic opponents despite representing a district won by former President Trump. Democrats see the race as an opportunity to compete in the Republican-dominated state, with the party believing it can be competitive in multiple Iowa contests this cycle.

cards.headline: Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Christina Bohannan set for House rematch in Iowa
cards.teaser: The race marks the third consecutive election between the two candidates.
cards.body:
Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Democrat Christina Bohannan won their respective primaries in Iowa's 1st Congressional District and will face each other again in November. Miller-Meeks defeated David Pautsch while Bohannan defeated Travis Terrell.

Bohannan is a former member of the Iowa House. This will be the third straight election pitting the two candidates against each other in the district.
